summary: Reporter's native label: BLOCKING. Claimed a real leak window if yuzu::win::to_wide() throws (evaluated as a constructor argument, before ScratchDirGuard's RAII body exists) after yuzu_create_temp_dir() already succeeded.
trigger: std::bad_alloc from a ~600-byte std::wstring allocation inside to_wide()
disposition_note: Independently verified agents/shared/win_str.hpp:74's to_wide(): never throws on empty/untranslatable input (returns {} instead), the ONLY throw path is std::bad_alloc from the internal std::wstring construction -- the exact same generic allocation-can-throw property every other RAII-by-value constructor call in this codebase already has (including to_wide() itself used the identical constructor-argument way elsewhere, e.g. win_profiles.hpp's RegOpenKeyExW(profiles.get(), to_wide(rec.sid).c_str(), ...)). Not a novel defect this diff introduced; treating it as such would require auditing every RAII constructor call in the codebase for the same theoretical OOM-during-construction property, which the codebase does not do anywhere else. Re-derived: I9 (no operational impact beyond the codebase's existing, universal OOM posture), E6 (the wrong outcome -- a leak from a sub-1KB allocation failing while a 256 MiB hive copy runs routinely in the same function -- is not a realistic production scenario).
adjudicated_by: Doomgoose (PR author -- NICE-severity de-escalation, no independent adjudicator required per Gate 7; the underlying facts are independently verifiable by reading agents/shared/win_str.hpp:74 directly)
adjudication_rationale: Reporter's native BLOCKING rests on a generic C++ allocation-failure property already present at every RAII-by-value construction site in this codebase, not a defect specific to this diff -- derived band corrected to match the actual facts (I9/E6) rather than the reporter's label.
